source.title: Cortical map reorganization enabled by nucleus basalis activity.

confidence_rationale: Canonical, high-source-quality (Science, Merzenich lab) demonstration that basal-forebrain cholinergic activity is what ENABLES adult cortical plasticity: pairing a tone with nucleus basalis stimulation drives massive auditory-cortex remapping, while the same acoustic input without NB activation does not. This is the direct biological referent for the OPENING-side gate MECH-398 proposes -- a basal-forebrain ACh signal that gates whether sensory input is incorporated into long-term cortical representation. Held at 0.80 (not higher) because the transfer is from a phasic electrical-stimulation paradigm in rat AI to an algorithmic learning-rate scalar in REE; the mapping is to the abstract gating role, not the cholinergic pharmacology.
failure_signatures: Receptive fields were narrowed, broadened, or left unchanged depending on the acoustic parameters paired with NB activation -- the gate does not impose a fixed plasticity direction; it licenses input-driven change. A REE gain scalar that merely scales a single global learning rate (rather than letting the paired input shape WHAT is learned) would under-represent this: the biology gates plasticity ON, the content of the change still comes from the input stream.

Plasticity required PAIRING (NB activation coincident with the stimulus); NB stimulation alone or stimulus alone did not remap. A REE gate driven by a state scalar that is not temporally bound to the to-be-learned input would mislocalise plasticity -- the gating must be coincident with the encoder's exposure to the input it should incorporate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Episodic electrical stimulation of the cholinergic nucleus basalis, paired with an auditory stimulus, produces progressive large-scale reorganization of adult primary auditory cortex; the basal forebrain plays an active instructional role in representational plasticity, marking which stimuli the cortex should incorporate.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-398 proposes a basal-forebrain ACh-analog plasticity-GAIN gate: a state-conditional scalar in [0,1] that multiplies encoder learning rates and residue write magnitudes, deciding WHEN representations update rather than WHAT they update to. Kilgard & Merzenich is the foundational evidence that such a basal-forebrain gating signal exists and is causally necessary for adult cortical plasticity -- without it the cortex still perceives and acts but stops remapping. This grounds the OPENING side of the plasticity window that REE currently lacks (it owns only the closure side: INV-074 / MECH-333 closure half / MECH-334).
mapping.mapping_caveat: The experiment uses exogenous electrical NB stimulation as a permissive teaching signal in adult rat AI; REE's analogue is an endogenously-computed gain scalar driven by surprise/salience/arousal proxies (MECH-205 / SD-032a / drive). The transfer is to the property 'a basal-forebrain gating signal licenses representational update', NOT to acetylcholine receptor signalling or to the specific auditory-map readout. The paper evidences the EXISTENCE and gating role of the opening-side signal (MECH-398); it does not by itself adjudicate the state-conditional architecture (ARC-093) or the closure clock (MECH-399).
mapping.source_context: Adult rat primary auditory cortex (AI); chronic NB electrical stimulation paired with tones; single-unit receptive-field mapping; in vivo.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality very high (Science, definitive paradigm). Mapping fidelity moderate-high: the gating ROLE maps cleanly, but REE's gate is an endogenous scalar not an exogenous stimulation. Transfer risk moderate: rat sensory cortex to an algorithmic encoder, and electrical-stimulation teaching signal to a computed state scalar. Aggregate weighted toward source quality and the clean gating-role mapping.
